name: LOL Galactic Title
epitaph: Billed in the fed's own founding FAQ (21 July 1998) as "the big one; the most prestigious title offered by the LOL," reserved for the very best. Won by Van Halent at the fed's own SantaSlam '98 season finale in November 1998, per its own later recap; Van Halent carried the belt through the fed's 1999 return, retaining it against every challenger the surviving record shows.

name: LOL Orange Grove Texas Title
epitaph: The fed's own secondary singles title, named after the birthplace of LOL boss Ronald Adonis per the founding FAQ (21 July 1998). Held by G.I. Slow entering the fed's 1999 return before he lost it on the fed's own 6 June 1999 broadcast to "The Loose Screw" Dmitri Damian Maku Stalin, who successfully defended it at the fed's own 20 June 1999 broadcast, the last of the surviving record.

name: LOL World Tag Teem Titties
epitaph: The fed's only tag team title, per the founding FAQ (21 July 1998), which notes a third title may be added later "should we develop a big enough roster." Unclaimed in every document held before the fed's 1999 return, it was finally awarded on 3 June 1999 to the Real American Zeroes by tournament; they lost it eleven days later to a pairing of Bubbolicious Bob and Van Halent, whose own partnership then broke up, and the fed's on-screen Chancellor held the belts up rather than let them be defended by a team that could not work together. A rematch to crown new champions, announced for 28 June 1999, falls after the end of the surviving record.
